name: Tribute - Generated Battle Pass / Season Track Screen
summary: Draws the battle pass screen from your own reward table: a season banner, a progress rail and drawn reward emblems in a free and a premium lane. Claim a reward and it redraws.
description:
Your game already has a reward table. Tribute draws the battle pass screen from it.

Hand Tribute a season (its name, its tiers, the free and premium reward on each tier, and the player's progress) and it composes the season track a live game shows its players: a season banner with its own motif, a progress rail, and one plate per tier in a free lane and a premium lane, each carrying a drawn emblem chosen from the reward's own name. Locked, claimable and claimed rewards each get their own treatment, so a player sees what is left to take without reading a label. The result is an ordinary Texture2D. Nothing on the page is an imported image: every emblem, banner, plate and letter is drawn in code by a software rasteriser shipped in the package, and the package ships no font.

61 HAND-AUTHORED EMBLEMS

51 reward emblems cover currencies, chests and crates, cosmetics, weapons and gear, consumables, pets and mounts, emotes, sprays and stickers, trophies and more. 10 season banner motifs cover snowflake, flame, leaf, wave, moon, crown, circuit, sun, skull and star. The emblem comes from the reward's own words, matched whole-word: "Epic Chest" draws a chest, "XP Boost" draws a bolt. A name the corpus does not know gets a stable emblem, never a blank.

WHAT YOUR DATA DOES TO THE SCREEN

The season's name picks one of seven liveries (Frost, Ember, Verdant, Tide, Dusk, Gilt, Neon) and the banner motif. A rarity word, in a Rarity field or in the name itself ("Legendary Skin"), colours the plate's rim in the colours players already read: common, uncommon, rare, epic, legendary, mythic. A reward whose words name no rarity keeps its lane's own rim, so nothing is guessed. Later tiers are richer: more coins in a stack, more points on a crown, more facets on a gem. The rail fills to the current tier, claimed rewards read pressed and spent, claimable ones get a halo, and locked ones are veiled with a padlock. A premium lane the player does not own stays locked. The editor window's derivation panel lists every choice with the word that made it.

BUILT TO BE RECOMPOSED

TributeTrack.Bake touches no Unity object, so it runs off the main thread, and TributeTrack.ToTexture uploads the result. Emblem tiles are cached, so claiming one reward redraws only the emblem that changed. Tiles are drawn on worker threads with byte-identical output. Long seasons are paged, and the default page holds the player's current tier.

GETTING STARTED

1. Import the package. Everything lands under Assets/CSAF/Tribute/.
2. Open Demo/Scenes/TributeDemo.unity and press Play. LEFT and RIGHT change season, UP and DOWN change page, C claims the next reward and redraws.
3. Assets > Create > CSAF > Tribute > Season makes a season you fill in the Inspector. Press Compose this season in Tribute at the top of it.
4. Window > CSAF > Tribute composes any season asset, pages through it, lists every emblem and rarity with the word that chose it, and saves a PNG.
5. From code, build a SeasonPass from your own reward table and call TributeTrack.Compose.

Tribute draws the screen. It does not store progress, grant rewards or talk to a server. Composition is CPU rasterisation, so compose when the season or the progress changes, off the main thread for anything a player opens, never per frame.
technical:
Features: battle pass / season track screen generated from your own reward table; 61 hand-authored emblems (51 rewards, 10 banner motifs) chosen by whole-word match on the reward's name with a stable fallback; seven liveries; six rarity rims; locked, claimable and claimed treatments; paging that opens on the current tier; thread-safe bake with a tile cache and parallel tiles; ScriptableObject season asset; editor window with a derivation panel and PNG export.

Number of C# scripts: 19 (17 Runtime, 1 Editor, 1 Demo). Visual Scripting graphs: 0.
Assemblies: CSAF.Tribute.Runtime (all platforms), CSAF.Tribute.Editor (Editor only), CSAF.Tribute.Demo (demo scene script).
Editor window: Window > CSAF > Tribute. Demo scene: Assets/CSAF/Tribute/Demo/Scenes/TributeDemo.unity.
Minimum Unity version: 2022.3. Built and tested against 6000.5.7f1.
Render pipelines: Built-In, URP and HDRP. The page is rasterised into a Texture2D on the CPU and never touches the render pipeline.
Target platforms: all platforms Unity targets. On WebGL the tiles are drawn on one thread.
Development platforms: Windows, Mac. Pure C#, no native libraries.
No Resources folder, no shaders, no images, no fonts, no network calls, no telemetry. Dependencies: none.
No third-party assets are included.

Documentation: https://github.com/onefreeman1337/csaf-releases/blob/main/docs/tribute/README.md
ai:
All of the C# in this package was written by an AI coding agent (Anthropic Claude) under human direction. That covers the software rasteriser, the drawn letterforms, the emblem and banner corpus, the season model and its derivation rules, the composer, the editor window and the demo scene.

The screens the package produces are not made by an image model. Every emblem, banner, plate and letter is drawn by the shipped code from authored geometry, offline. The store images are captures and composites of that output. Some of them, including the cover, set the package's own rendered output over an AI-generated illustrated background.

No audio is included, because the package contains no audio of any kind. Text and dialog: no.
